events.description: 9/11 shattered international inhibitions on CT cooperation; al-Qaeda plotted from Afghan safe haven
Roggio patrols with Iraqi troops in Mosul who fought al-Qaeda in Iraq
Islamic State declares the caliphate; second global wake-up call; 2014-16 peak of CT cooperation

Reports that Russia may be supplying missiles to the Houthis, facilitated by Iran

key_claims: The world is in a 'third era' of the jihadi threat: CT cooperation has collapsed (US-Russia rift, UN discredited), the West believes it has won, and state sponsorship of terrorism is reviving, led by Iran.
Al-Qaeda's leader Saif al-Adel is in Iran and al-Qaeda may be becoming part of Iran's axis of resistance; Iran has deployed al-Qaeda operatives and AQAP has a deconfliction with the Houthis.
The Taliban could become a state sponsor again; the Haqqani Network is intertwined with al-Qaeda, the TTP and the IMU, and the Taliban are edging toward regional recognition.
Pakistan is, per Roggio, the number two state sponsor of terrorism and still supports the Taliban.
The 2021 Taliban victory was a 'shot in the arm' for jihadists worldwide; JNIM and al-Shabaab seek to replicate it, and there are more safe havens now than before 9/11.

Russia and Iran ignored US pre-attack warnings before the Crocus and Kerman attacks, illustrating the collapse of CT cooperation; Russia is becoming a state sponsor by supplying missiles to the Houthis.
Fitton-Brown predicts a major al-Qaeda or ISIS mass-casualty attack in the West by end of 2025.
Of 40,000+ ISIS foreign fighters perhaps 25,000 remain alive, an unprecedented recidivism risk far larger than the post-Afghanistan legacy.
